name: Pease Pudding
author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors

ingredients.item: 1 uncooked ham hock or ham joint (from a butcher shop)

steps: Put the ham hock in a pressure cooker and cover with water.
With the lid on bring to the boil (full pressure).
Lower the heat and simmer for 30–40 minutes.
Remove from the heat and release the pressure. Take out the hock and put to one side.
With the lid on, bring back to the boil.
Again lower the heat to a simmer (as low as possible).
Remove from the heat and release the pressure.
Put the contents into a bowl with the butter, and mix with a balloon type whisk.
Serve on white bread or stottie cake, alone or with ham from the hock. Refrigerate when cool.

culture.text: Pease pudding, also known as pease porridge, is a savoury pudding dish made of boiled legumes, typically split yellow peas, with water, salt and spices, and often cooked with a bacon or ham joint. A common dish in the north-east of England, it is consumed to a lesser extent in the rest of Britain. In Newfoundland, it retains its traditional name as part of the customary Jiggs dinner. In non-English speaking countries, similar dishes exist under different names.
